'''''Catalpa ovata''''', the '''yellow catalpa'''<ref name=grin/><ref name=rp1>{{cite book |first=Roger |last=Phillips |title=Trees in Britain, Europe and North America |year=1978 |publisher=Pan Books Ltd. |location= Cavaye Place, [[London, England]] |page=96 |isbn=978-0-330-25480-9}}</ref> or '''Chinese catalpa'''<ref name=grin/> ({{zh|c=梓|p=zǐ}}), is a pod-bearing tree native to [[China]]. Compared to [[Catalpa speciosa|''C. speciosa'']], it is much smaller, typically reaching heights between {{convert|20|and|30|ft|m|0}}. The [[inflorescence]]s form {{convert|4|-|10|in|mm|adj=mid|-long}} bunches of creamy white flowers with distinctly yellow tinging; individual [[flower]]s are about {{convert|1|in|mm|0}} wide. They bloom in July and August.<ref name=rp1/> The [[leaf|leaves]] are very similar in shape to those of ''[[Paulownia tomentosa]]'', having three lobes (two are abruptly truncated on either edge, with a third, central, slightly acute, pointed lobe forming the leaf apex), and are darkly green.<ref name=rp1/><ref name=rp2>{{cite book |first=Roger |last=Phillips |title=Trees in Britain, Europe and North America |year=1978 |publisher=Pan Books Ltd. |location= Cavaye Place, London, England |page=42 |isbn=978-0-330-25480-9}}</ref> [[Fruit]]s are very narrow, foot-long [[Glossary of plant morphology terms#Fruit types|pods]].<ref name=rp1/>

Although native to the more temperate provinces within China ([[Anhui]], [[Gansu]], [[Hebei]], [[Heilongjiang]], [[Henan]], [[Hubei]], [[Jiangsu]], [[Jilin]], [[Liaoning]], [[Inner Mongolia|Nei Monggol]], [[Ningxia]], [[Qinghai]], [[Shaanxi]], [[Shandong]], [[Shanxi]], [[Sichuan]], [[Xinjiang]]),<ref name=grin/> ''C. ovata'' is also cultivated in North America and Europe, and has become a parent of ''[[Catalpa × erubescens]]'' with the American species ''[[Catalpa bignonioides]]''.<ref name=grin/><ref name=rp1/> It is commonly used to make the undersides of [[guqin|qin]].<ref name=yeung>{{cite book|first=Juni|last=Yeung|title=Standards for the Guqin February 2010 Draft|year=2010|publisher=Toronto Guqin Society|location=Toronto}}</ref>

==Chemistry==
The plant contains [[dehydro-alpha-lapachone]]<ref>[http://www.biobiopha.com/EnProductShow.asp?ID=2237 Dehydro-alpha-lapachone] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402183755/http://www.biobiopha.com/EnProductShow.asp?ID=2237 |date=2012-04-02 }}</ref> (DAL) which inhibits vessel regeneration, interferes with vessel [[anastomosis]], and limits plexus formation in zebrafish.<ref>Garkavtsev I, Chauhan VP, Wong HK, Mukhopadhyay A, Glicksman MA, Peterson RT, Jain RK.,"Dehydro-alpha-lapachone, a plant product with antivascular activity."  ''Proc Natl Acad Sci USA''. 2011 Jul 12;108(28):11596-601</ref> DAL also controlled the development of the fungi [[rice blast]], [[tomato late blight]], [[wheat leaf rust]], [[barley powdery mildew]] and [[red pepper anthracnose]] (''[[Colletotrichum coccodes]]'' (Wallr) S Hughes). The chemical was particularly effective in suppressing anthracnose.<ref>{{cite journal | pmid = 16550502 | year = 2006 | last1 = Cho | first1 = JY | last2 = Kim | first2 = HY | last3 = Choi | first3 = GJ | last4 = Jang | first4 = KS | last5 = Lim | first5 = HK | last6 = Lim | first6 = CH | last7 = Cho | first7 = KY | last8 = Kim | first8 = JC | title = Dehydro-alpha-lapachone isolated from Catalpa ovata stems: Activity against plant pathogenic fungi | volume = 62 | issue = 5 | pages = 414–8 | doi = 10.1002/ps.1180 | journal = Pest Management Science}}</ref>
